penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: A cross-BU token orchestration proxy or unified SFMC API layer requires per-customer setup, credential onboarding, and integration debugging — hands-on per client work that cannot be fully automated.

penalties_applied.name: requires_synchronous_human
penalties_applied.reason: Selling into enterprise Salesforce environments typically requires a scoping call or demo; self-serve signup is unlikely for credential management tooling touching production Salesforce orgs.

rationale: The buyer is a real enterprise SFMC developer or admin with genuine pain and an active Salesforce contract, but building the actual solution — a cross-BU API proxy or token orchestration layer — requires deep SFMC-specific integration work well beyond a Claude prompt plus a web form. Operational autonomy is low because each customer would need bespoke credential setup. The weighted total before penalties is already borderline and penalties from per-customer human work and required sales calls drop this to 2.6 — well below the validate threshold.
solution_plan: Not viable for this factory. A working SFMC cross-BU token proxy would require deep Salesforce Connected App integration, OAuth scope negotiation per BU, and likely ongoing debugging of Salesforce platform quirks — this is a full SaaS product, not a prompt-plus-Stripe service. A solo non-technical operator cannot build or maintain it without engineering resources. If the goal is a consultancy service (do-it-for-you credential setup), it could generate revenue but would be entirely Youval's hands-on billable time, which contradicts the autonomy requirement. Drop this path.
notes: Fails operational_autonomy_min (4 < 7) and buildability_with_ai_min (4 < 6). Even ignoring penalties, the total would not reach validate threshold after penalty deductions.
